Subject: End-of-quarter verdict: scoring reconciliation, impact vignettes, and rapid comms plan

Team —

Thanks for pulling together the evidence pack. I ran a pass on the proposed OKR scores and sketched a short narrative we can use in the QBR slide and for any customer comms. Two quick asks to close this out by EOD Tue (2027-04-20):

1) Confirm final score for OKR 2 (Model serving reliability): proposal in the attached evidence pack drops from 7 -> 6 because of the April 3 incident and lower-than-expected 99th percentile under burst tests. If we accept the reduction, we need a 1-2 sentence exec rationale.

2) Validate the customer impact vignettes for Acme Analytics in impact-vignettes.md (attached) — if those land, I will send a short RFC to Acme asking them to confirm impact language for the QBR.

I've attached: q2-okr-evidence-pack.pdf (full scoring table + artifacts), impact-vignettes.md (customer-facing drafts). Links to Drive and HubSpot are below.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/record/ACME-1234

Please reply with: final score decision (accept/reject), two-sentence rationale (if score changes), and any edits to the Acme vignette by EOD Tue. I will consolidate and route to Exec Review Wed morning.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. PM, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: q2-okr-evidence-pack.pdf (PDF stub), impact-vignettes.md (text)

Marissa —

Quick notes after scanning the pack: I agree with the proposed downgrade for OKR 2 (7 -> 6) given the reproducible latency spike and the customer incidents that map to it. Also concur with a 0.5-point soft reduction on OKR 5 (Throughput efficiency) where the quantization rollout missed the target.

Action items:
- Irene: please draft a 1-2 sentence exec rationale per changed OKR (why score moved, mitigation in place).
- Ben: once rationale is ready, add the finalized line to the QBR deck (slide 6) and flag any downstream metrics that need to be footnoted.
- Marissa: collect customer-facing vignette approvals; I want to see a single consolidated slide for Exec.

I am elevating the contested reliability sub-item (cache eviction behavior) to leadership review — include the debug trace in the evidence pack so Exec can see the telemetry.

Thx,
Vivek
VP, Product & Platform

Date: 2027-04-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-of-quarter verdict: scoring reconciliation, impact vignettes, and rapid comms plan

All —

I dug into the telemetry and customer tickets and put a short evidence summary below; this is pulled from q2-okr-evidence-pack.pdf (see section 3). I also drafted suggested rationale lines for Exec and a customer-facing blurb we can send to Acme.

Evidence summary (high level):
- April 3 incident: cache eviction bug coincident with a model patch. 3 customer incidents (Acme x2, BetaCorp x1) between 03:23–03:42 UTC; rolling restart mitigated the errors.
- 99th percentile latency: moved from baseline 210ms -> 430ms under a 10k rps burst test when KV cache warmed cold.
- Mitigations in place: hotfix patch 4/7 (reduces eviction frequency), backoff tuning deployed 4/10, expanded canary to 20% on 4/12.
- Residual risk: intermittent miss of warm-cache profile for new long-tail request patterns; incident recurrence probability estimated ~7% without further tuning.

Draft executive rationale (1-2 sentences):
"We adjusted OKR 2 downward to reflect an incident on April 3 that revealed a cache eviction regression under bursty workloads. Remediation work is deployed and reduces recurrence risk, but residual edge-case behavior justifies a conservative score pending the next validation window."

Customer-facing vignette for Acme (two-line suggestion):
"During early April load tests we observed intermittent latency spikes that affected a subset of inference requests. Our team deployed a hotfix and tuning changes; we validated improved performance in follow-up canaries and will continue to monitor Acme-specific traffic patterns during the next quarter."

I attached impact-vignettes.md with slight edits (minor tone-down of technical details). If this looks good I can push both rationale lines to Marissa and Ben to assemble into the QBR deck.

— Irene
Director, Applied ML
